With both sides desperate for points in the final stretch of the campaign, the atmosphere at the stadium was electric from the opening whistle, setting the stage for a physical and unpredictable encounter. A Cagey Opening at the Allianz Riviera The match began with both sides testing each other through set-pieces. Nice looked particularly dangerous early on, with Tom Louchet delivering several teasing corners that kept the Lens backline on high alert. In the 12th minute, a defensive blunder by Pierre Ganiou almost gifted the hosts an opener, but the visitors managed to scramble the ball clear. Juma Bah came closest for the home side in the 17th minute, rising highest to meet a Louchet cross, but his header was comfortably gathered by Robin Risser . Lens responded with pressure of their own, primarily through the delivery of Florian Thauvin , whose corners frequently caused chaos in the Nice penalty area. The game took a brief pause in the 21st minute as the referee consulted VAR for a potential penalty in favor of Nice , though play eventually resumed without a spot-kick being awarded. As the first half progressed, the contest turned increasingly physical; Malang Sarr was booked for unsportsmanlike conduct, and both Juma Bah and Florian Thauvin received yellow cards just before the interval as the intensity boiled over. Saint-Maximin Breaks the Deadlock The second half saw the deadlock finally broken in spectacular fashion. In the 60th minute, Adrien Thomasson found space in the middle of the park and threaded a pass to Allan Saint-Maximin . The mercurial forward, showing the flair that has made him a household name, unleashed a powerful left-footed strike from outside the box that beat the diving Yehvann Diouf to give Lens a 1-0 lead. The goal sparked a frantic response from Nice manager, who opted for a triple substitution in the 71st minute, introducing Ali Abdi , Isak Jansson , and Salis Abdul Samed to find a way back into the game. Lens looked to consolidate their lead, with Odsonne Edouard leading the line effectively before being replaced by Abdallah Sima . However, the momentum shifted dramatically in the 81st minute. Saud Abdulhamid , acting as the last man, committed a professional foul to stop a goal-scoring opportunity and was shown a straight red card. The dismissal left Lens vulnerable and forced them into a defensive shell for the closing stages. Late Drama and the Equalizer Capitalizing on their numerical advantage, Nice poured forward. The pressure told in the 84th minute when a loose ball in the box fell perfectly for the substitute Ali Abdi . The defender reacted quickest, stabbing the ball home with his left foot to send the home crowd into raptures and level the score at 1-1. The final minutes were played at a breakneck pace, with Adrien Thomasson receiving a yellow card for dissent as tensions flared between the players and the officials. In stoppage time, Nice pushed for a winner, with Kevin Carlos nearly connecting with a volley that flew just wide of the target. Melvin Bard was forced into a tactical foul to halt a late Lens counter-attack, earning himself a booking in the process. Despite the frantic end-to-end action and five minutes of added time, neither side could find a decisive third goal. The referee blew the whistle on a hard-fought draw that saw Lens finish with ten men and Nice walking away with a well-earned point thanks to their late resurgence.

Both sides showed a clear desire to claim victory, but resolute defending and a lack of cutting edge in the final third meant the deadlock remained unbroken for extended periods. A First Half of Tactical Battles The opening 45 minutes were characterized by a fierce midfield struggle, with both teams attempting to establish their authority. However, none of these deliveries resulted in concrete goal threats, as the respective defenses remained alert and organized. Possession was evenly shared, reflecting the balance on the pitch. Nice sought to build more elaborate attacks, while Metz appeared more inclined to exploit quick transitions, albeit without significant success. As the first half drew to a close, the referee awarded a goal kick to Metz following a corner from Nice , and the game entered halftime with the scoreline unchanged and everything to play for in the second half. Second Half: Tactical Adjustments and Increased Intensity The restart of the match saw tactical substitutions implemented by both teams, with Charles Vanhoutte making way for Hicham Boudaoui and Kail Boudache being replaced by Mohamed-Ali Cho for Nice . Metz also introduced fresh legs later in the game, with Alpha Toure leaving the field for Urie-Michel Mboula , and Jonathan Clauss being substituted by Kevin Carlos . These changes were aimed at injecting new energy and different attacking perspectives. Despite the substitutions, the game continued to be a tactical chess match. Both teams continued to exchange corners and probe for openings in the opposition's defense. Nice looked to press their advantage with corners from Mohamed-Ali Cho and Ali Abdi , while Metz responded with plays involving Gauthier Hein and Bouna Sarr . The match also saw some robust challenges, with yellow cards issued to Elye Wahi for a rough foul and to Boubacar Traore for pushing an opponent. Kojo Peprah Oppong also entered the referee's book for a strong tackle. Late Drama and Final Whistle In the closing stages, the tempo increased as both sides pushed harder in search of a match-winning goal. Nice saw Elye Wahi replaced by Tom Louchet , and Sofiane Diop made way for Isak Jansson . Metz also brought on Jean-Philippe Gbamin for Believe Munongo . Nice had a chance through Isak Jansson , whose shot was held by Jonathan Fischer . Metz also threatened, with Jean-Philippe Gbamin sending a effort wide. In the dying moments, Ali Abdi had a header that went narrowly off target, and Metz had their opportunities, but to no avail.
